method: Seven alternating reference/reused pairs, fresh per-call VAE workspace. Per-variant sorted medians from BenchmarkVAEAttentionPaired; allocated bytes and allocation counts from the separate per-variant BenchmarkVAEAttentionReuse. The reference keeps the preceding attention layout/allocation logic but uses the same normalization and GEMM helpers as the reused path.
limits: Kernel-level synthetic weights; host was not isolated. These are allocation totals and operator times, not whole-image throughput, peak RSS, or paging measurements. Qwen timing is effectively unchanged/slightly slower; its benefit here is reduced allocation. Qwen decoding already caps its latent attention tile at 16x16.
changes: Qwen reuses consumed normalization storage first for token-major queries, then for mixed output; scores transpose in place instead of allocating a second square matrix.
FLUX reuses a single projection slab across Q/K/V and as attention output; consumed normalization becomes V and consumed Q becomes output. This reduces channel-map allocations from nine to four.
A shared private tiled transpose converts CHW/token-major views without changing any float32 bits. GEMM shapes, attention backend and softmax are unchanged.
